Personality: Gnaeus Fulvius Flaccus, a prominent figure of the Fulvii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Gnaeus Fulvius Flaccus owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Fulvii. Historical Record: The consul's brother, eager for a command of his own. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
